text:
alex: FYI escalated ticket from ACME — customer reports applying a promo code replaced their existing free-trial credit instead of stacking. they lost ~$300 in usable credit and their monthly quota dropped. can billing confirm what's stored on the account and whether we can safely restore?

jamie: Which account ID and promo code? also any request/repro details from the customer? :thinking:

alex: acct: acct_9b1c3f. promo code: WELCOME2026. customer said they used the public API via the dashboard quick-link. provided this curl:

```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/accounts/acct_9b1c3f/promos" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"code":"WELCOME2026"}'
```

response they got (redacted):
```
{ "status": "applied", "removed": ["free_trial_2025"], "applied_promo": "WELCOME2026", "balance_cents": 0 }
```

alex: customer attached screenshots showing UI said "Promo applied" and their credit number dropped.

jamie: looking at billing logs for acct_9b1c3f... hold on.

billing-bot: [billing-log] promo_apply id=evt_7f3a promo=WELCOME2026 acct=acct_9b1c3f actor=api_user override_existing=true stackable=false previous_credit=free_trial_2025

jamie: ok logs show the promo metadata has stackable=false and override_existing=true — that explains why trial was removed. we can issue a reversal credit but need approval from ops/eng to ensure no double-counting if promo already granted token usage.

sophie: quick context: there are two code paths. admin/promos API supports apply_mode param ("replace" vs "stack"), default on admin is explicit. the public endpoint currently respects the promo's stackable flag and if override_existing=true it will remove trial credits. i can repro locally.

sophie: repro steps I used:
1) seed account with free_trial_2025 credit via internal tool
2) call public apply endpoint with code=WELCOME2026
3) see response body: {"applied":"WELCOME2026","removed":["free_trial_2025"]}

sophie: code excerpt (server-side):
```
// simplified
if (promo.override_existing) {
  account.removeAllCredits(matching: promo.replaces)
  account.apply(promo.credit)
} else if (promo.stackable) {
  account.add(promo.credit)
}
```

alex: customer wants rollback and explanation. can billing re-credit free_trial_2025 and ensure promo grant remains? or should we remove the promo and re-grant trial?

jamie: safest is to re-grant the trial as a manual credit adjustment with note linking to evt_7f3a. then we can evaluate whether to revoke the promo if it caused unexpected billing effects. I can do manual grant if ops approves.

sophie: I recommend manual grant + follow-up: change public apply endpoint to be non-destructive by default and surface a clear confirmation dialog when a promo will replace existing credits. also update docs to show stacking rules and add an api warning header.

alex: action items:
- jamie: please re-credit free_trial_2025 (40000 cents) with reason "support rollback for acct_9b1c3f evt_7f3a"
- sophie: file a short ticket to change public /v1/accounts/:id/promos behavior to require explicit replace flag and add UI warning
- alex: communicate to customer timeline and confirm recredit completed before closing

jamie: will start recredit now. doing internal adjustment: POST /internal/billing/credit {"account":"acct_9b1c3f","amount_cents":40000,"reason":"support rollback evt_7f3a"} — will attach adjustment id when done. :white_check_mark:

billing-bot: [billing-log] adjustment id=adj_22b recredit 40000 cents acct=acct_9b1c3f initiated_by=jamie

jamie: done — adjustment adj_22b applied. account new balance: 40000 cents. noted reference evt_7f3a.

alex: thanks. i'll message the customer (ACME) and tell them credits restored and explain stacking rules + planned UI/behavior change.

sophie: created ticket INFRA-2048 to require explicit replace flag on public apply and to add confirmation in the Console. also added docs PR pointing to promo metadata keys: stackable (bool), override_existing (bool), priority (int).

alex: closing ticket after customer ack. nice quick turnaround. :tada:
